studio.name: Studio HQ
studio.statusLine: All five research scouts are in. Four finalist niches are in deep-dive now. Nothing is built yet and no niche is chosen.
studio.killCriterion: If no niche reaches 10 paid founding deposits by the kill date, the venture stops and the studio picks a different market.

needsYou.title: Answer Gate 1: pick the niche
needsYou.why: Four candidates survived scoring. Your choice sets everything downstream: the rules engine, the landing page, the app. I have a recommendation ready.

needsYou.title: Optional: widen this environment's network access
needsYou.why: The environment's network policy refused connections to capterra.com, trustpilot.com, appfollow.io, apps.apple.com, reddit.com and every .gov host we tried, so all Phase 1 evidence is search-snippet only and no App Store competitive survey was possible. Open the cloud environment menu in the session title bar, choose Edit, and add those hosts under Allowed domains with 'Allow package managers' left ticked. Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#network-access

funnel.note: Targets are pre-committed in Phase 2, before any traffic arrives, so they cannot be moved to fit the result.

risks.risk: Phase 1 scouting missed paid competitors in at least one finalist niche, because the App Store could not be searched. The first deep dive found two.
risks.mitigation: Every finalist gets an App Store search by hand before any code is written, and a competitor that already computes the same thing is an immediate drop.

risks.risk: No primary source was readable. The environment's network policy refused every research host, so all Phase 1 evidence is search-snippet only.
risks.mitigation: Treat every penalty and interval figure as unverified. A domain expert signs off the rule set before launch, and the engine marks each rule verified, snippet-only or unverified.

risks.risk: No App Store competitive survey was possible, because apps.apple.com is refused. Competitive weakness scores are provisional.
risks.mitigation: You run four App Store searches by hand on your phone at Gate 1. Ten minutes, and it can kill a pick.

risks.risk: The recurring killer across 37 niches: whoever owns the data gives tracking away free. CE Broker, NCEES, NABP, SeaLog, Zoetis all do.
risks.mitigation: Only niches where nobody is already paid to track the dates survived. Re-test this for the chosen niche before building.

risks.risk: The shared web-search budget ran out mid-research, leaving parts of three clusters under-researched.
risks.mitigation: Named gaps are listed per niche in the raw scout files and re-run against the chosen niche only.

risks.risk: No Swift compiler in this environment. The first real compile happens in GitHub Actions on macOS.
risks.mitigation: Conservative stable-API Swift, a line-by-line adversarial review, and CI watched until green.

risks.risk: App Store rejection or liability from wording that reads as a verdict on legality or safety.
risks.mitigation: Every string passes the compliance wording test. We state the user's records and the public interval, never a verdict.

log.what: Deep dive done: 6/10. Paywall carve-out holds and reachability is the best of the four, but the price ceiling is about $60/yr and gear dates are entered once a year, so there is little to retain.

Deep dive done: 6/10. Found a 2024 FAR amendment that invalidates the case law both scouts anchored on, and that GSA's free emails are more accurate than ours would be. Only the wider recert portfolio survives.
Deep dive done: pursue conditional, 6.5/10. Corrected the qualifying-day rule (8 hours, not 4 hours underway) and found two paid competitors Phase 1 missed. Blue-ocean score cut from 4 to 3.
Four deep-dive analysts dispatched on the finalists. Equity windows added as a fourth because it tied the top weighted score.
Cross-border cluster done. Equity date windows score highest in that cluster; immigration killed as legal advice.
Studio HQ built. Ten agents appointed across five teams.
SMB cluster done. GovCon recerts and DOT small fleets survive; lien deadlines killed as legal advice plus Levelset.
Assets cluster done. Charter captains and show horses survive; classic cars killed because no deadline exists.
Wildcards done. Motorsport safety gear scores highest in any cluster; welders killed on a paywalled standard.
Credentials cluster done. Most killed: the data owner gives tracking away free.
Network policy refused every research host. Evidence quality downgraded to snippet-only and recorded as a risk.
Scoring rubric and hard gates locked before any scout reported.
Five research scouts dispatched across 37 candidate niches.
